Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.api

Class Mandela

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.api.Mandela
public final class Mandela extends Object
The one class a host needs to meet, and the single place the language's public identity lives.

Everything here is sugar over Runtime. That is the point: the embedding API is the same surface the CLI and the editor extension use, so a snippet in a guide is a snippet that actually runs, and a host cannot drift into a private corner of the implementation. A desktop app that wants to run a script writes two lines:


 Object total = Mandela.engine()
         .bind("tax", Interop.fn1("tax", amount -> ((Double) amount) * 0.15))
         .build()
         .run("price(100) + tax(100)");

Choosing a sandbox

engine() hands out Capabilities.console() — a console and nothing else, no files, no environment, no network, no threads, no JVM — because the failure mode of a default is a script that reaches something it should not have. A host that means to allow more says so on the builder, from the place that knows which document or applet asked for it:

  • Capabilities.console() — stdout and stderr only, the default;
  • Capabilities.webPage() — what a browser page script gets: computation with no console at all, since the page's own console is a host function;
  • Capabilities.desktop(java.nio.file.Path) — a real app whose files live under one root;
  • Capabilities.open() — everything, which is the mandela command line running a script its own author wrote and nothing an embedder should reach for;
  • Capabilities.builder() — a host with its own policy, which is what Espresso's per-project trust decision is.

Three doors, one engine

A host picks whichever door fits its language and its build. This class is the Java and Kotlin door. MandelaScriptEngine is javax.script, so a tool that already embeds JSR-223 finds Mandela with new ScriptEngineManager().getEngineByName("mandela") and needs no new dependency. And the mandela command line is the same runtime launched from a shell, which is what makes a script testable before anything embeds it.

    • eval

      public static Object eval(String source)
      Runs one program in a throwaway engine, printing to System.out.

      The convenience call for a test, a one-liner and a documentation example. It runs in Capabilities.console() — it cannot touch a file, the environment, a socket or a thread, so nothing here needs a capability decision; anything that does should build an engine and keep it.

      Parameters:
      source - the program
      Returns:
      the value of its last expression
      Throws:
      MandelaError - when the script fails
      LangException - when it does not compile

    • eval

      public static Object eval(String source, Map<String,Object> values)
      Runs one program with host values already bound.

      Each value goes through Interop.toMandela(java.lang.Object), so a Java List, Map, String, number or lambda is usable directly and the host does not have to convert first.

      Parameters:
      source - the program
      values - the names to bind before running
      Returns:
      the value of the program's last expression

    • check

      public static List<Diagnostic> check(String source)
      Reports what is wrong with a program, without running it and without throwing.

      The editor's diagnostic line and mandela check both read this, so an IDE-quality answer needs no engine, no capabilities and no side effect.

      Parameters:
      source - the program text
      Returns:
      the findings, empty when the program is sound

    • scriptEngine

      public static ScriptEngine scriptEngine()
      The JSR-223 engine, for a host that already speaks javax.script.

      Uses the platform's registry, so it works when the jar is on the classpath like any other script engine; scriptEngineDirect() is the same engine for a host that cannot rely on the registry (a shaded jar, a modular launch, an applet with an odd loader).

      Returns:
      a fresh engine
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - when this jar's service registration is missing

    • scriptEngineDirect

      public static ScriptEngine scriptEngineDirect()
      Returns:
      a fresh JSR-223 engine, built directly rather than through the registry
